newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares shed earlier mild gains on Monday to end slightly weaker as a softer start to Wall Street and thin investor participation weighed on the market.
The AEX index of blue chip stocks closed 0.91 points easier at 674.77, after hitting an earlier peak at 676.47.
"It was a very dull day and the market is stuck with a wait-and-see attitude," one dealer commented.
Sagging financials sapped the index's strength and banking groups ING and ABN AMRO both lost ground to finish the day 0.50 and 0.60 guilders down at 68.80 and 120.50 respectively.

But the star performer was semiconductor equipment maker ASM International, which at one point had surged more than 20 percent. It ended off its intra-day high of 35.50 guilders but was still 3.40 guilders up at 31.60 by the close.

Analysts said the stock had been sought after on Friday by U.S. investors, who were confident over the future for semiconductor companies. This had led to further buying by Dutch investors today, dealers added.
Dutch broker Wesselius issued a buy recomendation on the stock late last week saying it was well placed to benefit from the growth in the sector in the second half of 1997.
Philips put on a late spurt to end 1.40 guilders higher at 75.40 but elsewhere there was little activity of note.

Chart analysts were also predicting the market could be set for a period of range-bound trading, having broken down through a rising trned channel recently. "This triggered a range between 666 and 686 points. We exepct this range to remain intact this week," an analyst at IRIS said.
Others were looking for a break above 686 points for the previous uptrend to be resumed. At the same time, unless the strong support at 670 gave way, downside potential was limited.
